def _combine_regex(*regexes: str) -> str:
    """Combine a number of regexes in to a single regex.

    Returns:

    return "|".join(regexes)


class Highlighter(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for highlighters."""

    def __call__(self, text: Union[str, Text]) -> Text:
        """Highlight a str or Text instance.

        Args:
            text (Union[str, ~Text]): Text to highlight.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If not called with text or str.

        return highlight_text

    @abstractmethod
    def highlight(self, text: Text) -> None:
        """Apply highlighting in place to text.

        Args:

        """


class NullHighlighter(Highlighter):
    """A highlighter object that doesn't highlight.

    May be used to disable highlighting entirely.

The character set `[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]` seems to be the part that defines valid URL characters.

If a URL contains a tilde (`~`), it is not included in this character set.

The fix should be to add `~` to this character set.

The test failed: `AssertionError: assert [Span(1, 31, 'repr.url')] == [Span(1, 28, 'repr.url')]`.

The expected span length was 28 characters (from `https://example.com/~user/path`).
The actual span length was 31 characters.

Let's count the characters in the input string: `" https://example.com/~user/path "`
1 (space) + 27 (url) + 1 (space) = 29 characters total.

The URL itself is `https://example.com/~user/path`.
Length of this URL:
`https://example.com/` (20 chars)
`~user/path` (10 chars)
Total length = 30 characters.

Wait, the input string in the test case is:
`" https://example.com/~user/path "`

Let's count the characters in the string literal:
` ` (1) + `h`...`p` (29) + ` ` (1) = 31 characters.

The regex matches the URL part.
The URL is `https://example.com/~user/path`.
The match should start at index 1 (after the leading space) and end at index 31 (exclusive, so length 30).

If the input string is `" https://example.com/~user/path "`, length is 31.
The match starts at index 1.
The match should end at index $1 + 30 = 31$.

The test case I added was:
`(\" https://example.com/~user/path \", [Span(1, 28, \"repr.url\")]),\n`
The expected end index is 28. This is incorrect. It should be 31.

The actual output from the test run was:
`[Span(1, 31, 'repr.url')]`
This means the regex successfully matched the entire URL, including the tilde, and the span correctly identified the start (1) and end (31).

The error is in the expected span definition in my test case. I need to correct the expected end index from 28 to 31.

I will modify the test case in `tests/test_highlighter.py` again.
